image.description: Generated editorial illustration; not an architecture figure or experimental data.
image.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: wide editorial illustration for a personal engineering blog about editing a music model's weights to make a piano request produce flute.
Primary request: a carefully composed, tactile illustration connecting a piano keyboard, a small matrix of blue and rose squares, and a silver concert flute. This is conceptual cover art, not a technical diagram.
Scene: pale cool paper background, almost white #f4f5fb. A cropped close-up piano keyboard enters from the lower left. Fine graphite construction lines and a few delicately printed square matrices occupy the center. A realistically recognizable silver transverse concert flute, complete with keys and lip plate, extends across the upper right. Small blue and rose cells appear to bridge the two instruments. A visual thought about changing a few numbers to change sound.
Style: sophisticated mixed-media editorial collage, precise graphite drawing with restrained gouache and subtle paper grain. Intelligent, spare, slightly playful; closer to a musician's working notebook than sci-fi AI imagery. Detailed physical instruments, generous breathing room.
Composition: wide landscape 3:2. Large enough instruments to read at a 700-pixel blog width. No text anywhere. No people, no robot brains, no neon, no gradients, no watermarks, no logos, no floating musical-note clipart. Limit accent color to ink blue #4b45dc and a small amount of dusty rose; black and silver instrument details. High quality publication illustration.

audio.note: Byte-identical copies of the level-matched generated outputs. These clips use text conditioning, not an external reference recording.
